Chapter 3: Trusting God Through Uncertainty and Change
Change—it's one of those things that’s always with us, isn’t it? Sometimes, it sweeps in like a breath of fresh air: a new job, a move to a new city, or just a chance to start over. Other times, though, change can feel like a rug pulled out from under you. Loss, disappointment, a plan that suddenly vanishes. And in those moments, trust can feel pretty fragile.
You might find yourself lying awake, mind spinning with questions. What’s coming next? Will things ever settle down? If you’re honest, you might feel a bit lost, just searching for something steady to grab onto.
That’s where daily prayer comes into the picture. Trusting God isn’t a one-and-done thing—it’s something you choose again each day. Every morning, you’re invited to hand over your worries, your plans, and all those unknowns. Some mornings, trust just flows. Other days, it’s a struggle.
Let me tell you about a man going through a huge career change. He’d always liked being in control, but suddenly, the future was wide open—and not in a good way. The fear was real. So every day, he brought that anxiety into prayer. Sometimes he had the words, sometimes he just sat in the quiet. And slowly, something shifted. He realized trusting God wasn’t about having all the answers; it was about knowing he wasn’t alone while he waited.
Or think about a young woman dealing with a tough relationship. She’d been hurt before, so letting herself trust again? That felt risky. In her prayers, she poured out her doubts and fears. And she found comfort in old stories from Scripture—stories of people who faced their own uncertainty and still found God’s faithfulness. Those words became her anchor. She discovered that trust isn’t about never feeling afraid. It’s about choosing to show up, day after day, even when you’re scared.
Most of us don’t realize just how much energy we spend trying to control things we can’t. Prayer offers a different path. It’s not about giving up, but about having the courage to let go. When you name your fears, even for a moment, and release them, you find a surprising kind of strength.
This journey isn’t a straight line. There are ups and downs, doubts, and plenty of days when trust feels out of reach. But the daily rhythm of prayer gives you space to be real—to bring your questions, your faith, and your doubts. Over time, trust stops being about certainty, and starts being about relationship. It’s that quiet confidence that, no matter what changes, God’s presence doesn’t.
So, daily prayer becomes this balancing act: letting go of your grip on control, and holding tight to the promise that Jesus is right there with you—guiding each step, even when you can’t see where the path leads.
